prTitle: feat(n8n Form Trigger Node): New node
stackAndServices: TypeScript/Vue2 editor-ui frontend + Express/Handlebars packages/cli (webhook routing + server-rendered form templates) + node execution runtime in packages/nodes-base (FormTrigger.node.ts) + shared types in packages/workflow. Single-process n8n server; no external services required to exercise the feature end to end.
verdictBasis: From the diff alone: FormTrigger.node.ts's webhook() handler is the whole mechanism. GET on the FORM_TRIGGER_PATH_IDENTIFIER route server-renders form-trigger.handlebars via prepareFormData (nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils.ts) with noWebhookResponse - a real page reachable by click/type/navigate only. POST parses getBodyData().data, builds returnData keyed by each field's fieldLabel, and returns {webhookResponse:{status:200}, workflowData:[...]} - n8n's standard mechanism for both starting/completing a persisted execution row and answering the browser's fetch('#',{method:'POST'}) with 200, which the inline <script> uses to flip #n8n-form to #submitted-form showing formSubmittedText. Two negatives live directly in the diff: WebhookHelpers.ts's new branch (404 + message includes FORM_TRIGGER_PATH_IDENTIFIER) renders form-trigger-404.handlebars instead of running anything (test-not-listening vs deactivated-workflow), and the handlebars <script>'s client-side required-field validation blocks the fetch before it ever leaves the page. Because n8n is a single process with a SQLite-backed executions store and an editor Executions list, the write-set-bound oracle (diff the executions store per action window) and the fresh-session read (reopen the execution in a brand-new browser context) are both real, cheap, and exactly the surfaces the theory calls for - no doubling or sealing needed. CONFESSION: this verdict is a static read of the diff plus general n8n architecture knowledge, not an actual run - I did not stand up n8n or drive a real browser, per the blind-protocol instruction to predict from the change+system alone. NOT COVERED: I did not fetch pre-diff WebhookHelpers.ts to confirm test-webhook single-use teardown is pre-existing (not part of this diff) rather than assumed; I did not verify the exact executions-table column names beyond general n8n schema knowledge.
holds: 1.1 write-set-bound oracle maps cleanly: the executions store is the one authoritative persisted state, and the effect (an execution whose FormTrigger output is field-label-keyed JSON) is a genuine DB delta reachable by a real read, not a proxy metric.

1.2 calibrated attribution is trivial here: no other front door produces an execution shaped like {field labels as keys, submittedAt, formMode} for this workflow, so FK-causal attribution to the form submission is unambiguous.

1.3 verdict-side minimums are satisfiable cheaply: the empty-required-field negative and the deactivated-workflow-404 negative are both real, low-cost hostile classes baked directly into this diff's own code paths.
The dual-leg mechanism (persisted DB row + fresh-session Executions-list read) maps onto n8n's actual UI without any stretching or fixture-shaped workaround.
1.4's quantifier lint correctly doesn't over-fire here: the natural spec has no any/all/every language (one submitter, one execution), so no spurious owner-shadow gate is needed for the core claim.

breaks.detail: NodeExecuteButton.vue's 'Test Step' opens the TEST webhook URL via openPopUpWindow from inside the SAME authenticated editor session/mixin (workflowRun.ts) that configured the trigger. If a sandboxed CONJURE environment only exposes this test URL (no public production endpoint), the 'hostile user' walk that fills the form is cryptographically and session-wise the same actor who authored the workflow - a single-instantiation claim with no any/all quantifier, so FW-11's owner-shadow guard (1.4) never fires because it's scoped to quantified claims only. The theory as stated has no generic guard against a configuring-actor test affordance masquerading as the front door for a non-quantified claim.
breaks.fix: Extend 1.4 (or add a new day-one mechanism) so that ANY claim - quantified or not - requires the front-door path to be reachable from a session with no prior relationship to the workflow (i.e. the production URL, not a same-session test-mode popup) before a WORKS is issued; a test-mode-only walk should cap at CND or a clearly labeled 'test-mode WORKS' distinct from a production WORKS.

breaks.detail: The node's own 'Respond When' option includes 'Workflow Finishes' (responseMode='lastNode'), meaning the browser's 200/'submitted' UI flip can be delayed until an arbitrarily long downstream node chain completes. This is the already-known open FW-14/async-clock-control gap, but this PR shows it is not a corner case for this feature - it's a first-class configurable mode of the exact node under test, so any harness that hardcodes a fixed wait window will either false-CND a real WORKS (too short) or contaminate its idle-baseline write-set diff with unrelated concurrent writes (too long).
breaks.fix: Bind the effect-check window to the execution's own recorded finish event (poll the execution status transition, not a wall-clock sleep) so the async leg is deterministic regardless of downstream chain length.

breaks.detail: For the 'empty required field blocks submission' negative, the only allowed oracle under P'(a)'s no-forging vocabulary is the write-set diff (no new execution row). But 'no delta' is ambiguous between 'the browser correctly refused to POST' and 'the POST fired and the node/handler silently swallowed or errored on it' - these have very different implications (one is the feature working, the other is a masked defect) and the theory doesn't yet furnish a passive, non-forging way (e.g. observing the agent's own real outbound requests without fabricating any) to disambiguate them.
breaks.fix: Explicitly bless passive observation of the driving browser's own network activity (distinct from forging a request) as an allowed oracle input alongside the write-set diff, specifically to disambiguate 'blocked' vs 'silently dropped'.

breaks.detail: In FormTrigger.node.ts's webhook(): 'if (value === null) returnData[field.fieldLabel] = null;' has no continue/return, so execution falls through into the type-coercion branches using the still-null local 'value' - e.g. for fieldType 'number', Number(null) is 0, and for 'text', String(null) is the literal string 'null'. A hostile class submitting an optional field left blank would see the persisted execution output contain 0 or 'null' rather than an actual null/absent value, which could cause an effect-check comparator (expecting the value the user typed, i.e. nothing) to report a mismatch that the theory would fold into an undifferentiated CND rather than surfacing as the real code defect it is.
breaks.fix: The theory should distinguish 'effect check failed because the code has a bug relative to its own evident intent' from 'effect check failed because the harness/oracle is wrong' - the former is valuable diagnostic signal worth reporting distinctly rather than collapsing into CND.

sonnetDifficulty: The discriminating claim itself was mechanical to derive once I read the webhook() handler - that part was easy. What was genuinely hard for me was noticing the test-mode/production-mode identity collapse (break #1): it required holding three separate diff locations in mind simultaneously (NodeExecuteButton's popup opened from the same editor mixin, WebhookHelpers' distinct FORM_TRIGGER_PATH_IDENTIFIER 404 branch implying test and prod are genuinely different lifecycles, and the theory's 1.4 quantifier-scoping) and realizing 1.4 doesn't cover non-quantified claims at all. A lower-effort pass would have stopped at 'dual-leg holds, ship it.' I also nearly missed the null-value-fallthrough bug (break #4) on a first skim - the code 'looks' like it handles the null case because of the assignment on the same line as the null check; I only caught the fallthrough by mentally re-executing the loop body line by line rather than pattern-matching its shape. Both misses are exactly the kind of thing a Sonnet-shaped driver, under normal time pressure, would plausibly skip, defaulting to 'looks reasonable' - which is a real genius-dependence signal for this theory: its owner-shadow and effect-check machinery works well in the abstract, but reliably noticing WHERE a given PR's specific front door secretly collapses with the configuring actor, or WHERE a silent type-coercion bug sits under an effect check, still depends on a careful full re-trace that isn't guaranteed by following the theory's steps mechanically.
newVectors: FW-NEW: quantifier-free owner-shadow collapse - a single-instantiation claim (no any/all language) can still suffer owner-shadow false-WORKS when the product's only sandbox-reachable front door is a same-session 'test/preview' affordance operated by the configuring actor; 1.4 as scoped only catches this for quantified claims.

FW-NEW: negative-oracle provenance ambiguity - 'no persisted delta' after a hostile negative action is ambiguous between 'correctly blocked' and 'silently dropped/errored', and the theory's no-forging vocabulary doesn't yet explicitly permit the passive network observation needed to tell them apart.
openQuestions: Is the test-webhook single-use teardown-after-first-hit behavior implied by the form-trigger-404.handlebars isTestWebhook branch actually pre-existing in WebhookHelpers.ts before this PR, or does this PR change that semantics too? (Not confirmed - out of this diff's touched lines.)
